m_tlul_if.sv

suspected_bugs.what: Not a bug in normal use, reported for the reviewer. w_load is gated by the TL-UL FSM being IDLE, but the APB FSM goes to BUSY on w_req_launch whether or not the TL-UL side loaded the request. If a launch ever came while the TL-UL FSM was not IDLE, the APB FSM would wait in BUSY for a response to a request that was never issued, and the transfer would hang. The invariant 'TL-UL FSM is idle whenever the APB FSM is idle' (BR-5.4-06) should make this case unreachable, so I kept it unchanged.

Observation only. BUSY -> DONE (and so PREADY) depends only on i_resp_valid; i_apb_psel and i_apb_penable are not checked. BR-3-18 (PREADY only in an Access cycle) therefore holds only if the APB requester keeps to the protocol. I kept the behaviour as it is.

open_points: RR-40: PARA_SRC_ID is a 32-bit typed parameter, and only bits [PARA_SRC_W-1:0] are used (now through localparam LPARA_SRC_ID). The original does the same. If some Verilator version reports the unused upper bits of the parameter, the only fixes are a lint waiver or a change to how the parameter is compared. Comparing the full 32 bits would change behaviour for out-of-range PARA_SRC_ID values, so I kept the bit-select.

BR-3-33 / BR-8-09 (illegal parameter values reported at elaboration) is not in the original RTL, and I did not add it. An elaboration check would have to be simulation-only code or $error, and RR-11 forbids system tasks in synthesizable RTL; it belongs in the verification source set.
notes:
I rewrote all three files and kept the original names, so nothing is removed. The logic and the state encoding are the same as in original/, so the outputs should match cycle for cycle. I have not run the formal equivalence check, Verilator lint or Yosys.

What changed:
- **m_tlul_if:** LPARA_A_SIZE, LPARA_A_MASK and LPARA_D_ACK_DATA moved from the parameter port list into the module body. They now have exact widths (2, 4 and 3 bits) with the same values, so the old [1:0], [3:0] and [2:0] selects of 32-bit constants are gone. A new localparam LPARA_SRC_ID holds PARA_SRC_ID[PARA_SRC_W-1:0], which is the same bit-select the original used, so the values are unchanged.
- **Top module:** the default of PARA_SRC_ID is now written as 0 instead of '0; the value is the same. All other parameters, defaults and port names, directions and widths are unchanged. The port order is also the original one.
- **Lint waivers:** the unused inputs i_apb_pprot, i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink and i_tlul_d_user are each wrapped in a `verilator lint_off/lint_on UNUSEDSIGNAL` pragma. Each pragma has a `// WAIVER:` comment on the line before it (DEC-006, DEC-007).
- **Readability:** every single-statement if/else now has begin/end.
- **Headers:** each file header now states the module's purpose and the specification sections it implements.
- **Requirement tags:** I added `// REQ:` tags using only IDs from REQUIREMENTS.md.
- **Resets:** every register keeps its asynchronous active-low reset and its reset value; the original had no unreset registers. There was no simulation-only code in the original.
